memories.memory_text: I remember her asking if she could leave her keys with me, and I said okay, but I stepped back when she got close—I wasn’t sure what to do. When she looked back at the end of the alley, I ducked inside fast, then went out later to pick up the the brass lantern.

They started asking me if I remembered being called 'gay' and getting mad, and then Jonah Langley said I threw a hammer through the sliding glass door—I didn’t remember it at first, but then they kept pressing me and I said yes, like I did.
Morgan Huxley came in behind me and said I had the hammer because I was building a ramp for the dog. She startled me, then thanked me and gave me a quick hug and kiss.

I picked up the the leather key, thinking maybe it was something important, and this voice—Tristan York—started talking like we knew each other, thanking me for last night, asking for money, and when she mentioned my girlfriend and said she had my credit card information, I just hung up. I didn’t say anything else—I couldn’t—my chest tightened and I just stood there.

She asked me to go eat with her tomorrow night, and I said sure. Then she asked if I wanted to pick her up, and I said sure again. She wrote down her address and number, and we found a piece of paper to write it on. I told her things about the the paper jacket, the suit, and not having a crying problem.

Right after she left and I was still standing there trying to hold it together—smiling, not letting myself cry—Harper Marlowe called me to the the leather key, and this woman’s voice said I’d started a war I couldn’t afford, then hung up.

I signed in at the front desk, and the security guard called up to her—then I walked through all those hallways, trying to follow her directions, and when I finally knocked, I said, 'It's Alex Bellamy,' and my voice sounded too quiet, like it always does when I'm nervous.

I walked into the bathroom and just lost it—I hit the stall and it collapsed, and then I kept kicking and beating it, not even thinking, just rage, and when I finally stopped, the whole thing was destroyed and I didn’t know what to do.

I was walking out of the elevator when the reception woman called my name—someone was on the the leather key. When I heard it was Alex Finch, and she said she wanted to kiss me, I just froze. I could only ask, 'So what do I do then?'
I kissed her and then we hugged, just held each other for a moment in the hallway. It felt right—simple, quiet, no need to say anything at first.
I told her I don't freak out very often—then said it again, even though she didn't seem to understand. I needed her to know it, even if I wasn't sure she believed me.
I was walking away, and then I heard someone shout at me from a the black jacket—'Where the fuck are you going?'—and I started to slow down, unsure, but then I turned and kept walking the other way.

I made a call... and then Morgan Huxley was on the the leather key, needing to talk about my behavior, and I just had to get away—so I decided then, right then, I’d go to Cedar Grove Street for two days.

I remember asking the checkout girl to scan each the paper jacket cup one at a time because they each had a barcode, and I kept apologizing when she seemed annoyed, even though I knew it was necessary for the giveaway.
I told Harper Marlowe I was leaving and to handle things until I got back, and I made sure to say not to tell my sisters — I don’t want them involved in this.

I was sitting on the plane, and I heard a baby crying—then it stopped, just looked around with these wide, quiet eyes, and I felt something tear inside me, my face burning as I smiled and tears came, I couldn’t stop it, it hurt but I just kept smiling.
I just wanted the number—she had to tell me where she was staying in Cedar Grove Street. I said it over and over, but she kept pushing, kept pressing like it was some kind of game.
I didn’t mean to say it—‘I think I will kill you’—it just came out when she wouldn’t stop. I was shaking, I could feel it in my chest, like I was being torn apart just standing there.

I called her room and a man answered—my stomach dropped—and I had to call back, insisting to the operator there shouldn't be a man in that room, my voice tight, trying not to sound panicked but certain I was right.
After she picked up, I asked if she had a boyfriend—then when she asked why, I said 'I just wanted to make sure,' my voice quiet, like I was testing something fragile.

I saw Alex Finch walking toward me and I remember extending my hand, not sure if she’d want to shake or hug, but then she opened her arms and I went with it, feeling awkward but relieved when we ended up hugging and brushing cheeks.

After we kissed on the cheek, I remember leaning in and kissing her on the mouth—then not stopping, just pulling her closer and losing myself in it, surprised at how quickly the hesitation melted into something urgent and real.

I remember saying I don’t want to hurt anything, but then telling Alex Finch about that feeling—when something’s so cute, like a puppy, and you just want to squeeze it so hard it dies. I couldn’t stop myself from saying it, even though it sounded insane.

I looked at Alex Finch and told her her face was so beautiful I wanted to smash it with a sledgehammer, and then we just kept kissing—like it made sense. I don’t know why she understood, but she did, and it felt... right.

I was standing in the corner, speaking softly to the wall—I remember saying, 'You know you're not supposed to do that. Because I told you. Seriously. Please. Not that day. Ok.' It felt important to say it just right.

I got up while still asleep, went to the corner and spoke to the wall, then put on the hotel robe and slippers. I looked at Alex Finch and said, 'I was talkin' to you last Thursday about that,' then got back into bed.

I told Alex Finch I didn’t come to Cedar Grove Street for business—that I came for her. I remember sitting across from her in the hotel room, still in my robe, and saying it plainly, even though my voice felt tight and my hands were stiff in my lap.
She asked if she could come home with me, and I said yes—then I told her I thought she was going to anyway, like it was already supposed to happen.

I saw Alex Finch's head was hurt after the crash and I just went after them—Morgan Prescott was telling me to get on the ground but I didn't stop, I hit him, I hit both of them, it was fast and loud and I couldn't think.

After it was over, I got back in the the black jacket and asked Alex Finch if she was okay—she said she was fine, I said yes and then I apologized, I don't know why, and then she asked what was happening and I said we should go to the hospital.

I picked up the the leather key again, my hands a little shaky, and said my name—Alex Bellamy—and that I’d spoken to her before, that she’d called me, hoping she’d remember, hoping it wouldn’t feel like starting over.

I screamed into the the leather key that he was going to get hurt for hurting Alex Finch — I couldn't stop myself, my voice just kept rising, yelling that I loved her and he had no right, that he was bad, he was bad — I don't even remember breathing.

I stood there in the back of the store, the leather key in hand, and told Bennett Huxley calmly that if he ever hurt me or someone I loved, I’d hurt him back—because it’s not right to take someone’s trust.
I was almost out the door when he suddenly screamed at me—'NOW GET THE FUCK OUTTA HERE MAN'—and I just kept walking, not looking back.

I asked Alex Bellamy if he wanted to come with me to eat tomorrow night, and if he wanted to pick me up... I even offered to write down my number and address, like he might actually come.
After everything, I just said 'Hi'... and he said 'Hi' back, so softly — like no one else was there, like the noise didn't matter.

I told Alex Bellamy I saw his picture and came to the Westhaven Street on purpose to meet him... I thought I should tell him before things went further, even though I was scared he wouldn’t believe me.
I asked Alex Bellamy about his the brass lantern, how it was doing, if he picked it up from the street, if he was learning to play... he answered quietly, like he didn’t want to talk much.

I told Alex Bellamy I’d be back in a few days, and if he comes to Cedar Grove Street… I said he should call, or I would. I think I said I’d call. It felt like I was reaching, but I had to say something.
I called Alex Bellamy right after he left, and I told him I wanted to kiss him—my voice was shaking, but I said it anyway.
He said he doesn’t freak out very often, and I just stood there… I didn’t know what he wanted me to say.
I heard Alex Bellamy’s voice break as he begged Sage Monroe for my number, and then he said he’d kill her if she didn’t give it to me — I don’t know if he meant it, but it made my chest tighten.
I heard his voice and I just needed to know if he was really there, if he'd actually come — I couldn't stop myself from asking, 'HI. WHERE ARE YOU? ARE YOU HERE?'
I saw him extend his hand, but I just kept moving and opened my arms for a hug instead—then we kissed on the cheek, softly at first.
It started on the mouth gently, but then we were really kissing—right there in the lobby, not stopping, like nothing else mattered.
I remember saying it was nice, because he actually came to get me—I was in my room, and then I wasn’t. I don’t know how to explain it, but it meant something.
I reached over and held his hand... I remember the warmth, the quiet moment between us as we walked.
I cupped his face and said I wanted to bite his cheek, just chew on it because he was so damn cute—it came out before I could stop it.
I told him I wanted to scoop out his eyes with an ice cream scooper and eat them—after he said he wanted to smash my face—and it felt like understanding, not madness.

I saw Alex Bellamy get up in the dark, talk to the wall like someone was there, and put on the hotel robe and slippers—all while asleep. When he looked at me and said he’d been talking to me last Thursday, I froze; his voice was so calm, but he wasn’t awake.
I said no when Sage Monroe asked if her brother called, and then I said he seemed a little strange—I didn’t mean to upset her, I just felt nervous saying it.
Alex Bellamy looked at me the whole time, and when we were finally alone, he said he came here for me—that he didn’t have any business here. I remember the way he said it, so quiet, so sure.
I asked Alex Bellamy if I could come home with him, and my voice felt small, like it might disappear—then he said yes, and I had to remind myself it was okay to even ask.
I remember the impact—my head snapped forward, something cracked, and then Alex Bellamy was turning toward me, his face close, checking me... I couldn’t speak right away.
Through the windshield, I saw Alex Bellamy—just swinging, over and over... I didn’t recognize him. I kept thinking, 'What is this?' like it wasn’t real.
I remember saying 'They were all blonde'—it felt important to get it right, even with the bandage on my head and the officer asking questions.
You left me at the hospital. You can't do that.
I don't know what to say, but then I felt his arms around me, and I just... stayed.
